=== FIX-A — LANDING-POINT MISS RECONCILE (iter655 Q3, score 1.75) ===

QUESTION SHAPE: "first AND last status per ticket in one row" — TWO values of `status` per `ticket_id`, ordered by `changed_at`.

iter655 Q3 RESPONDER BUG (verbatim): wrote `first_value(status) OVER (PARTITION BY ticket_id ORDER BY changed_at)` + `last_value(status) OVER (... ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING)` COMBINED WITH `GROUP BY ticket_id`. INVALID — the window functions reference `status` / `changed_at`, neither of which is in `GROUP BY ticket_id` nor wrapped in an aggregate. Per the Trino SELECT-GROUP-BY analyzer rule (trino.io/docs/467/sql/select.html: "When a GROUP BY clause is used in a SELECT statement all output expressions must be either aggregate functions or columns present in the GROUP BY clause"), this fails the analyzer. Window functions are NEITHER aggregates NOR grouping columns — they cannot reference ungrouped columns under GROUP BY.

=== DOCS-TRUTH VERIFICATION (trino.io/docs/467, WebFetch on 2026-06-08) ===
• min_by(x, y) — "Returns the value of x associated with the minimum value of y over all input values." AGGREGATE function (listed under General aggregate functions). Produces one result per GROUP BY group. Ties on y: docs do not specify tie-breaking; result is arbitrary among tied rows. ✓ (matches resource framing verbatim)
• max_by(x, y) — "Returns the value of x associated with the maximum value of y over all input values." Symmetric AGGREGATE function. Same tie behavior. ✓
• first_value() / last_value() — listed under Window functions / Value functions. WINDOW functions (operate within a defined window). Default frame per Trino docs (verified): RANGE UNBOUNDED PRECEDING — which means `last_value` defaults to current row's value, NOT partition-last value, so an explicit `ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING` frame override IS required for partition-last (the iter655 responder got that frame override right). ✓
• SELECT-GROUP-BY rule (trino.io/docs/467/sql/select.html): "When a GROUP BY clause is used in a SELECT statement all output expressions must be either aggregate functions or columns present in the GROUP BY clause." Window functions are neither aggregates nor grouping columns; they cannot reference ungrouped columns under GROUP BY. ✓
